items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Ed Small called me, too, and told me every Sunday he wanted me to come in there with Dixie.

ctx.x: We went down there, and the guy wanted me to put a band in there. I told him I -- he said, oh, this is just for Sundays, a couple of hours. We need some music and all like that. So they finally convinced me. No music, didn't need any. The fellows I chose knew everything. They knew everything. And I had five men in there, and we just played regular dixieland stuff, like that.

Ed Small called me, too, and told me every Sunday he wanted me to come in there with Dixie. Now, that meant that I worked twice on Sundays, afternoon and night. Well, when you keep that up, gradually -- of course, I was at home, getting my meals there, but gradually it'll tell on you later on. You can't feel it, you don't realize it, because you're happy, carefree.

And I had a pocketful of money and I had put a little money in the bank, and the family was living comfortably and I was happy. All right, here come a call from Chick Webb, opening up at the Savoy. No, no, I'm ahead of myself. Fats Waller, Fats Waller, in between, called me. Come to the Capital. Well, I had been visiting there, because when the place opened,
